text.en: A seed and a small stone look alike. Plant both in soil with water. After a week the seed sprouts. The stone does not. What makes something alive?

Living things share certain characteristics. They need food, they breathe, they grow, they respond to changes, they reproduce and they die. A stone or a toy does not show these characteristics, so it is non-living.
Living things need food, water, air and a place to live (habitat). Plants make their own food using sunlight. Animals get food by eating plants or other animals.
A seed needs water, air and a suitable temperature to germinate, which means to sprout. The root grows down and the shoot grows up, and the plant grows bigger over time. Plants respond to light, and many plant parts grow toward it. Touch-me-not leaves fold when touched.
A plant's life cycle goes from seed to seedling to plant to flower to fruit with seeds. Many animals change form as they grow. A butterfly goes from egg to caterpillar to pupa to butterfly. A frog goes from egg to tadpole to frog. A mosquito goes from egg to larva to pupa to adult, and these early stages live in water.
Living things respond to stimuli like light, sound, touch and temperature. They reproduce to make more of their kind and all living things eventually die.

It does not, so a flame is not living.

prompt.en: Explain how you would prove that a seed is living.

requiredIdeas.en: Plant it with water and air.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking moving things are always living.
Thinking a plant does not respond.

points.en: Living things need food, breathe, grow, respond, reproduce and die.
Seeds need water, air and warmth to germinate.
Life cycles can include big changes in form.
